'''David A. Sánchez''' (born January 13, 1933) is a Mexican-American<ref name=AccentBook/><ref name=UBCpress/> university and research administrator, mathematician, educator, and author.  He held the posts of [[Provost (education)|provost]] at [[Lehigh University]], assistant director for the  [[National Science Foundation]] and  [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]],<ref name=LehighPastProvosts/> and assistant [[Chancellor (education)|Chancellor]] for the [[Texas A&M University]] (TAMU) system; As a mathematician, his areas of focus include [[ordinary differential equations]] and [[biomathematics]].<ref name=ResearchGate-DAS/> He has been a researcher and professor at several universities, including the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison|University of Wisconsin]]'s Mathematics Research Lab, [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], and the [[University of New Mexico]]. He published his memoir, ''Don't Forget the Accent Mark: A Memoir'', in 2011.<ref name=AccentBook/>

==Biography==
===Early life and education===
David Alan Sánchez  was born on January 13, 1933, in [[San Francisco]], [[California]] to Berta Sánchez.<ref name=AccentBook/>  At the age of three, he moved to [[Mission Hills, San Diego|Mission Hills]] in [[San Diego, California|San Diego]] and was [[adoption|adopted]] by his grandparents, Cecilio and Concepcion Sánchez.<ref name=AccentBook/>

Sánchez earned his [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in 1955 from the [[University of New Mexico]].  After graduating, he served the [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine Corps]] for three years.<ref name=AccentBook/>

Sánchez continued with his graduate studies at the [[University of Michigan]] (UM), where he worked at their Institute of Science and Technology in the Radar Laboratory. His research involved battlefield simulations for the [[United States Army|Army]].<ref name=AccentBook/> He received his [[Master of Science]] (M.S.) in 1960. He wrote his doctoral dissertation, ''[[Calculus of Variations]] for Integrals Depending on a Convolution Product '' under the direction [[Lamberto Cesari]]; receiving his [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]] (Ph.D.) in 1964 from UM.<ref name=MathGen-DAS/>

===Personal life===
In 1957, Sánchez married Joan Thomas. They have two children - a son and a daughter.<ref name=AccentBook/> After he retired from the University of New Mexico, he made his home in [[Corrales, New Mexico]].<ref name=UBCpress/>

==Career==
===Academia===
After completing his Ph.D., Sánchez spent two years at the [[University of Chicago]] as an instructor, before traveling to [[Manchester, England]] as a visiting professor at [[Manchester University]].

'''UCLA (1966–1977)'''<br>In 1966, Sánchez became an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA). While at UCLA, he presented papers at the American Mathematical Societies 1967 meeting, and at the Conference on Qualitative Theory
of Nonlinear Differential and Integral Equations in 1968, on extremals of composite functions and Ricotti equations, respectively.<ref name=Sanchez-SIAM-1966/><ref name=Sanchez-AMS-1968/> After four years, spent a year at [[Brown University]] as a visiting professor (1973–1974); and then returned to UCLA as an associate professor.<ref name=LehighPastProvosts/>  He became a full professor at UCLA in 1976.<ref name=AccentBook/>

''' University of New Mexico (1977–1986)'''<br>
In 1977, Sánchez returned to his undergraduate alma mater, the University of New Mexico, as a full professor in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. He served as the department chairman from 1983 to 1986). He took a [[sabbatical]] in 1982 to teach at the [[University of Wales]] in [[Aberystwyth]], [[Ceredigion, Wales]].<ref name=LehighPastProvosts/><ref name=AccentBook/>

In 1986, Sánchez took a nine-year detour in his academic career, into administrative roles.

'''Final posts - Texas A&M and University of New Mexico'''<br>
In 1995, after serving as assistant Chancellor for Texas A&M, Sánchez returned to a teaching and research role at the university.<ref name=NRM-2003/><ref name=Dipstick/><ref name=ResearchGate-DAS/>

Sánchez' returned to the University of New Mexico (UNM) for his final university position before retiring. At UNM, he served as chairman of the Department of Mathematics and Statistics.<ref name=UBCpress/>

===Administrative career (1986-1995) ===
In 1986, Sánchez took a detour from his traditional academic path to a new career path, accepting a position as the vice president and [[provost (education)|provost]] at [[Lehigh University]] in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=Lehigh1986/> While at Lehigh, he restructured the promotion and tenure process; and, chaired a commission on racial diversity.<ref name=LehighNSF/><ref name=LehighCommission/> He remained at Lehigh until 1990, when he moved to the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) to take a two-year term as an assistant director.<ref name=LehighNSF/><ref name=LehighPastProvosts/> At the NSF, he headed the Mathematics and Physical Sciences Directorate,<ref name=NSFbudget-1992/> the largest division at the NSF,<ref name=LehighNews-NSF/> "setting national priorities on scientific research."<ref name=LehighNSF/><ref name=AMSnotices1990/>
At the end of his term at the NSF, he took a position as an assistant director for the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].<ref name=LehighNSF/><ref name=LehighPastProvosts/>

In November 1993, Sánchez moved to the [[Texas A&M University]] System as Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs, to take on long-range planning.<ref name=AccentBook/> His foray into administration lasted for nine years, when he returned to teaching at Texas A&M.<ref name=Dipstick/>{{efn-ua|"For nine years he acquired a severe case of administrativitis, but recovered and is happily teaching at Texas A&M University." - P. Littleton<ref name=Dipstick/>}}

==Advocacy==

Sánchez participated, along with [[Richard A. Tapia]], in a panel discussion &mdash;  "Mexican-Americans and mathematics, or Where have all the Chicanos gone!" &mdash; at the 1980 annual meeting of the American Mathematical Society.<ref name=AMS-1980/>

==Selected publications==
Sánchez is the author of three books on mathematics and has written over fifty journal articles in the fields of [[mathematical optimization|optimization]], biomathematics, differential equations, and numerical analysis.<ref name=MathSciNet-DAS/> Here is a selected list of his publications:

===Books===
*{{cite book|year=1982 |first1=David A. |last1=Sánchez |first2=William D. |last2=Lakin
|title=Topics in Ordinary Differential Equations
|isbn=0486616061|publisher=Dover Publications}}
*{{cite book|year=1983 |author=Sánchez, David A.
|title=Differential Equations:An Introduction |edition=1st
|publisher=Addison Wesley Publishing Company
|isbn=0201077604}}
:*{{cite book|year=1988 |author=Sánchez, David A.
|title=Differential Equations |edition=2nd
|publisher=Addison Wesley Publishing Company
|isbn=0201154072}}
* {{cite book|year=2002
|title=Ordinary Differential Equations: A Brief Eclectic Tour|author=Sánchez, David A.
|series=Classroom Resource Materials |volume=19
|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|location=Washington, DC
|isbn=0-88385-723-5}} (a brief guide to concepts of ordinary differential equations)
*{{cite book|year=2012
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ii-oDwAAQBAJ
|title=Ordinary Differential Equations and Stability Theory: An Introduction |author=Sánchez, David A.

===Journals===

* Sánchez, D. A. (1964). "Total Variation and Uniform Convergence". ''The American Mathematical Monthly'', 71(5), 537–539.<ref name=Sanchez-AMM-1964/>
* Sánchez, D. A. (1966). "On Composite Variational Problems". ''SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics'', 14(1), 60–64.<ref name=Sanchez-SIAM-1966/>
* Sánchez, D. A. (1968). "On Extremals of Composite Variational Problems". ''Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society'', 19(3), 555–559.<ref name=Sanchez-AMS-1968/>
* Sánchez, D. A. (1969). "A Note on Periodic Solutions of Riccati-Type Equations." ''SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics'', 17(5), 957–959.<ref name=Sanchez-SIAM-1969/>
* Sánchez, D. A. (1975). "The Green’s Function and Determining Equations". ''The American Mathematical Monthly'', 82(7), 747–749.<ref name=AMM-1975/>
* Sánchez, David (1975). "Constant Rate Population Harvesting: Equilibrium and Stability". ''Theoretical population biology'', 8, 12–30.
* Lehmer, E., & Sánchez, D. A. (1980). "Problems Dedicated to Emory P. Starke: S27-S28". ''The American Mathematical Monthly'', 87(3), 218–218.<ref name=Lehmer-1980/>
* Sánchez, D. A. (1998). "Review of Ordinary Differential Equations Texts". ''The American Mathematical Monthly'', 105(4), 377–383.<ref name=AMM-1998/>
* Sánchez, D. A. (2001). "An Alternative to the Shooting Method for a Certain Class of Boundary Value Problems". ''The American Mathematical Monthly'', 108(6), 552–555. https://doi.org/10.2307/2695711
* Littleton, P., & Sánchez, D. A. (2001). "Dipsticks for Cylindrical Storage Tanks--Exact and Approximate". ''The College Mathematics Journal'', 32(5), 352–358. https://doi.org/10.2307/2687307
* Sánchez, David. (2008). "Periodic environments and periodic harvesting". ''Natural Resource Modeling'', 16, 233–244.
